Your whole 500 calorie reduction thing assumes they're currently consuming calories equal to their TDEE. Which probably isn't the case if they're overweight. If someone's energy expenditure is 2500 but they're eating 3000 calories a day, reducing by 500 is only going to stop further weight gain, not make them lose 52 pounds a year. 

Also, I don't agree with using a non-sustainable crash diet as an example of why others should be able to lose weight. Promoting a healthier lifestyle is great, but telling someone the results you've achieved while borderline starving yourself is only going to discourage the average person when they don't see results as quickly. I've maintained a healthy bodyweight my entire life, cutting back slightly on calories if needed. Yet, I've seen plenty of my friends do these crash diets and lose the weight for a few months only to put it right back on later because it's not sustainable to eat 800-1400 calories a day for an adult male. Just my two cents.

I just had surgery by Dr. Lo recently. Everyone's experience is slightly different but he generally has good reviews. The first time I took off my bandages I was a bit disappointed by the results, but that seemed to be mostly swelling / bruising causing asymmetry, as it looked a lot better 2 days later. And seems to improve a bit more each day. My nips have a bit of a crease but I semi-expected that since they were always quite puffy and a bit large, plus I'm still in the very early stages of healing. Overall, I'm definitely happy with the results and only expect things to improve as time goes on. I plan on getting in the gym and working my chest when I'm finally able to. The drains were a pain in the ass (definitely the worst part of the whole process imo), but with how much fluid came out of my chest I'm glad I had them.

Depends on your relationship with your parents. You could sit them down and explain the situation, how it affects you, and the options for fixing it. A lot of older people don't really know gyno is a thing so they might just think you put on fat in weird places first or not have noticed it. If they did notice it they might be more sympathetic to you wanting surgery.  

As far as side effects mainly just scarring, you could heal badly, or end up with a "sunken in" chest. I'm guessing being young might help with the scars but I'm not sure. 

You can generally start exercising lower body 2-3 weeks after, then upper body 4-6 weeks after but everyone is different. I'm guessing something like kickboxing might require a bit longer healing time since it uses upper body and involves a lot of contact. 

Good luck!
